task.description: Write a regression test suite for lib/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures.ex (net-new module, security- and idiom-reviewed, PASS at both gates). Follow the existing test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs as your structural model for testing a Mix.Task in this codebase (how it isolates from real repo state, how it invokes the task's internals directly rather than shelling out to `mix` itself, how it fakes/stubs any external command dependency). This module's core logic (tracked_issues/1 parsing docs/issues/*.yaml github_issue fields via regex, classify/1 deciding ZERO_EVIDENCE vs OK from a decoded gh JSON payload, grandfathered?/1 membership check) should be testable WITHOUT a live network call to `gh` -- design your tests to exercise the pure/testable functions directly with fixture data (fabricated docs/issues/ fixture files in a tmp dir, and fabricated gh-JSON-shaped maps/structs passed directly to classify/1), not by invoking the real `gh` CLI. Because this is a net-new module, a fail-then-pass regression test is only meaningful via MUTATION TESTING per docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md's 'When the pre-fix failure is non-existence' section (read it -- it is binding on this step): mutate the shipped classify/1 and/or grandfathered?/1 logic in at least 2 targeted ways (e.g. treat a closed issue with comments=0 but a real linked PR as still a violation; treat comments>0 as sufficient even with a self-contradicting/empty comment body; invert the grandfathered?/1 membership check) and record which of your tests fail against each mutant, proving your suite discriminates correct from wrong. Apply mutants in a throwaway git worktree (preferred, per WF-03's Isolation technique) or revert-and-verify in place per that same section's rules -- do NOT leave a mutant in the tree. Write the test file to test/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures_test.exs. Do NOT run the suite yourself (TEST-RUNNER's job) beyond what's needed to prove the fail-then-pass mutation results. Complete this handoff: status PASS/FAIL, result.summary (record each mutant and its pass/fail counts, and confirm the mutation revert was verified -- git status --porcelain empty, re-run green), artifacts_out, next_action ('Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR'). Claim by setting status to IN_PROGRESS only.
acceptance_criteria: test/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures_test.exs created, covering tracked_issues/1 parsing (all real docs/issues/*.yaml github_issue field shapes: bare integer, bare URL, quoted URL, null/absent), classify/1's ZERO_EVIDENCE vs OK decision, and grandfathered?/1 membership
Tests use fixture/fabricated data, not a live gh network call
At least 2 mutants applied to shipped logic, each mutant's per-test pass/fail counts recorded in result.summary, demonstrating the suite is sensitive to each specific trap
Mutation applied via throwaway worktree OR reverted in place with git status --porcelain empty AND a green re-run, both verified and quoted
No mutant left in the tree at handoff completion
